name: SmartChunk Evaluation Rubric
dataset: Synthetic test corpus; real-world generalization is not implied.

metrics.name: Structural integrity
metrics.definition: Fraction of source table, list and fenced-code blocks whose complete normalized text appears in at least one generated chunk.

metrics.name: Size compliance
metrics.definition: Fraction of output chunks not flagged oversized; this is a size check, not an accuracy score.

metrics.name: Source metadata coverage
metrics.definition: Fraction of chunks containing both source filename and source location.

metrics.name: Expected source/topic Hit@3
metrics.definition: For each labelled single-source question, whether a relevant chunk for the expected source and topic appears among the top three results.

metrics.name: MRR@20
metrics.definition: Mean reciprocal rank of the first expected source/topic match within the top twenty lexical retrieval results; zero when none appears in the ranked results.

metrics.name: Evidence Coverage@k
metrics.definition: Fraction of manually labelled required evidence text spans found in the top-k retrieved chunks.

metrics.name: Evidence Completeness@k
metrics.definition: Fraction of multi-evidence questions for which all annotated required evidence spans are found in the top-k retrieved chunks.

metrics.name: Processing time
metrics.definition: Median observed chunking time over repeated local runs; environment and settings must be recorded.

metrics.name: Mutation assertions
metrics.definition: Whether required text remains present, intentionally removed text is absent, and structural invariants remain satisfied for a controlled input mutation.

metrics.name: Security warning signal
metrics.definition: Whether the current normalizer reports a security-specific warning for a labelled suspicious fixture. No warning is not evidence of safety.

fair_comparison: Use the same source document, chunk size, overlap and question set for both strategies.
Manually verify every expected evidence span against the source document.
Report improvements, regressions, oversized chunks, warnings and unsupported capabilities.
Do not interpret lexical retrieval metrics as semantic retrieval or generated-answer accuracy.
Do not claim a security scanner exists if the application does not expose security-specific warnings.
Record the Git commit, environment and command used for every published report.
